answer: Persistent history bridge. Each agent identity carries an append-only action log whose head is co-signed by every counterparty it transacts with, forming a chain that any peer can verify. A duplicate clone cannot present the same log without an echo of the original's signatures, which the verifier flags as divergence. Attacker cost: fabricating a fresh log requires a crystal-clear gap in cosigners, forcing payment of real transaction fees and counterparty verification per identity, so N clones cost N times the genuine onboarding work.
